title: A subset nowhere dense in an open subspace is nowhere dense in the whole space

standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of a nowhere dense subset as one whose closure has empty interior, together with the behaviour of closures under passage to an open subspace
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on nowhere dense sets, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the property to be transferred and the closure computation used in the proof.

core_obligations: Assume an interior point: the proof supposes that a point of the ambient space is an interior point of the closure of the subset, witnessed by an open neighbourhood contained in that closure (proof lines 4247-4250).

Intersect with the open subspace: the intersection of that closure with the open subspace is the closure of the subset computed inside the subspace, so the open neighbourhood restricts to one contained in that closure (proof lines 4250-4252).

Contradiction with nowhere density in the subspace: the restricted neighbourhood would then be an interior point of the closure in the subspace, which is impossible, and the author closes by noting that such a point cannot lie in the closure of the subset (proof lines 4252-4253).
Conclusion: the subset is nowhere dense in the ambient space (proof line 4253).
proof_roadmap: 反设存在 x 是 T 在 X 中闭包的内部点，取开邻域 V ⊂ cl_X(T)。
则 V ∩ U 是 U 中的开集且 V ∩ U ⊂ cl_U(T)（闭包与开子空间相交即子空间中的闭包），与 T 在 U 中无处稠密矛盾。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement transfers nowhere density from an open subspace to the ambient space (author lemma at source lines 4238-4244, label lemma-image-nowhere-dense-open). The proof (source lines 4246-4254) is a contraposition computed with closures: an interior point of the closure in the ambient space would restrict to an interior point of the closure inside the open subspace, using that intersecting the closure with the open subspace gives the closure there (proof lines 4247-4253). H2.
